In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a set of scales designed to measure individual interaction characteristics in small group situations.
the development of an interaction profile for the individual in a small group situation.
the analysis of individual interaction characteristics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the findings reported herein indicate the existence of a factor structure which is similar to that reported in the Carter ( 2) study.
the three factors identified in the study by Carter ( 3 ) and replicated in the study reported here are not the only factors which account for individual differences in behavior in the small group.
the factor analysis of rankings made on trait names and behavior descriptive categories yielded results which were in general agreement with those of Carter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the utility of a factor analytic approach to the study of individual interaction characteristics in small groups.
the individual is not a unitary entity but a complex of interacting dimensions, each with its own set of characteristics.
the results obtained are consistent with those obtained in the Carter studies and that they are also consistent with other work in the field.
